headline: Sales and margins grow, sequential dip is normal seasonality
summary_short: Burlington's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 14.1% y/y to $2,856.5M (down 21.7% q/q against the holiday quarter), with net income up 13.8% y/y to $114.7M and diluted EPS up 13.3% y/y to $1.79 as gross margin expanded to 44.1%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 14.1% y/y to $2,856.5M on 127 net new/non-comparable stores plus 6% comparable-store sales growth, though it fell 21.7% q/q against Burlington's much larger holiday quarter. Gross margin expanded to 44.1% (from 43.8%) on better merchandise margin and freight costs. SG&A held flat at 34.7% of sales; a $15.3M inducement charge tied to a March 2026 convertible-note exchange was a one-off drag on operating income, which still rose 20.5% y/y to $167.7M. Net income rose 13.8% y/y to $114.7M and diluted EPS 13.3% y/y to $1.79. Cash fell to $747.4M (from $1,232.5M at fiscal year-end) after $193.6M of capex and $134.3M of treasury-share purchases. No new company guidance was given in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Net sales rose 14.1% on $196.9M from 127 net new/non-comparable stores opened since Q1 FY2025 plus 6% comparable-store sales growth adding $155.3M, per the MD&A.
Gross margin rose to 44.1% from 43.8%, which the filing attributes primarily to improved merchandise margin and lower freight costs.
SG&A held flat at 34.7% of sales as occupancy and sourcing-cost gains offset higher incentive pay and marketing; a $15.3M note-exchange inducement charge was a one-off drag.
Not separately explained for the GAAP figure; management's own Adjusted EBITDA (up $38.2M) cites higher sales and improved gross margin as the cause, which likely applies here too.
Rose on higher sales and increased gross margin rate, per management's own stated reason, despite the $15.3M debt-inducement charge and a $0.8M impairment charge.
Follows net income's rise; diluted share count was nearly flat (64.1M vs 64.0M y/y), so almost all of the per-share gain reflects the net-income increase.

Management frames the quarter as sales- and merchandise-margin-driven growth, with product-sourcing costs improving 30bp and its chase-the-trend buying strategy supporting flexibility amid a value-conscious, cost-pressured consumer.
